name: Say Hello: From Usenet to Slack
description: Fifty years of chatting across wires: email, newsgroups, chat rooms, instant messengers, texting, WhatsApp and the workplace apps that followed.

checkpoints.name: Mail and news
checkpoints.note: Email appears on the ARPANET, bulletin boards and Usenet let strangers share news and arguments by modem, and communities such as The WELL show that people can feel at home online.

checkpoints.name: Chat rooms
checkpoints.note: IRC brings live conversation to the net, while services such as CompuServe and AOL bring the public online. Chat rooms become a new place to meet people from anywhere.

checkpoints.name: Instant messengers
checkpoints.note: ICQ, AIM, Yahoo and MSN Messenger give everyone a buddy list and a way to know who is online. Hotmail makes email free, and teenagers spend evenings talking in tiny windows.

checkpoints.name: Texts and voices
checkpoints.note: Gmail, Skype and Google Talk make mail and calls free, while text messages and the BlackBerry's BBM spread among phone users. Facebook adds its own chat.

checkpoints.name: Apps for everything
checkpoints.note: WhatsApp, WeChat, Line, Telegram and iMessage put chat on every phone, Discord and Slack bring it into games and work, and privacy tools such as Signal offer encrypted talk.
